description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:2686-2688 — in §6.1.5(g)(iii)(3):
  `// Delete the leaf anyPolicy node.`
  `tree.retain(|nd| !(nd.depth == leaf_depth && nd.valid_policy == OID_ANY_POLICY));`

This deletion happens AFTER materialising nodes for initial_policy_set OIDs. This is the correct ordering per RFC 5280 §6.1.5(g)(iii)(3)-(4).

However, the materialization (lines 2676-2685) adds new PolicyNodes but does NOT populate their expected_policy_set from the parent anyPolicy node's expected_policy_set. It uses `expected_policy_set: vec![*p_oid]`. For newly materialized nodes at leaf depth, expected_policy_set is only used for the leaf level's own linkage (not needed beyond the leaf). So this is fine.

The deletion at line 2688 could leave a parent at depth leaf_depth-1 with anyPolicy in its expected_policy_set but no anyPolicy child at leaf_depth. The prune in §6.1.5(g)(iii)(4) at line 2692-2694 would then remove that parent if it has no other children. This is correct behavior.

Not a bug — the code follows the RFC algorithm correctly.
title: pkix-path chain_walk §6.1.5(g): leaf anyPolicy node deleted before materialising initial_policy_set
